name: Sam Williamson
headline: Building tech that helps people learn.
intro: I built a Mandarin learning website that's now part of my school's curriculum and ran a STEM camp for three years. The rest of my work, like the robots, prints, and repairs, is mostly me learning by building things.
school: USC Iovine + Young Academy, Arts, Technology + the Business of Innovation, Class of 2030
location: Los Altos, CA → Los Angeles, CA

bio: Hi! I'm Samantha Williamson, Sam for short. I grew up in Los Altos, in the Bay Area, and I study Arts, Technology and the Business of Innovation at USC's Iovine and Young Academy.
I am passionate about innovative ideas, hands on work, and developing meaningful connections with people!
facts: The lathe is my favorite machine to use.
I adopted a possum named Fred (he was set free).
Geography is cool and I am very good at GeoGuessr.
I have a dog named Wrigley.

projects.title: FRC Contributions
projects.summary: As president, I led a 120+ person team, one of the top 20 FIRST Robotics teams in the world. I ran a lot of projects in my time there; here are a few of my favorites.

links.label: Week Zero coverage, Mountain View Voice

projects.title: Mandarin Learning Website
projects.summary: I took four years of Mandarin class. I could read and write almost fluently but I still couldn't follow a conversation.

projects.title: Spartan Robotics Camp
projects.summary: A one-week LEGO SPIKE Prime camp for grades 3–8, written as a business plan and pitched to a sports camp that had never taught STEM.

links.label: Business plan + results (PDF, not in the bundle)

projects.title: Festival of Lights Floats
projects.summary: I work for the City of Los Altos on the floats for the Festival of Lights parade. I build them, design them, and run the sound and lighting on them. It is the parade I grew up watching in my own hometown.

projects.title: Foosball Table
projects.summary: A six-person engineering capstone at Mountain View High School. We built a full-size foosball table out of plywood, 3D printed the players, and wired an Arduino scoreboard into the cabinet. It lives in the lobby of the Student Services building.

projects.title: Lissajous Darkroom Prints
projects.summary: Two perpendicular waves draw a curve that disappears as soon as the sound stops. I exposed six songs onto photo paper with a laser so the shapes stayed.

video.title: Lissajous curves drawn by a laser

projects.title: CRT TV Guitar
projects.summary: A CRT television, an Arduino, and a fretless ribbon neck cut from birch. Sound comes out of the TV speaker; the notes show up as bars on the screen.

projects.title: Pinball Restoration
projects.summary: Williams Whirlwind, January 1990. My dad brought this machine home but it was completely out of order.
